newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - July 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The June-quarter Consumer Price Index released yesterday by the Australian Bureau of Statistics reveals prices fell by 0.2 percent between April and June and that Australia's annual inflation rate has dropped to a record low of 0.3 percent. The news has increased speculation of another cut in official interest rates. Page 1.

The Mortimer review of industry has recommended a A$21 billion, five-year plan to reform the Commonwealth's business assistance strategy. The report also advises the Federal Government to target 3.4 percent annual per capita economic growth over the next decade to ensure the economy keeps pace with those of Asia. Page 1.

Fear of being displaced from their position before having implemented their plans for the organisations they head, is the biggest fear of Australian chief executives according to a survey conducted by International management consultants Price Waterhouse Urwick. Despite this 86 percent of those surveyed said they focused on long-term solutions to problems instead of using stop gag measures such as downsizing. Page 1.

The Federal Government was embarrassed again yesterday by the leaking of a second confidential briefing document on the South Pacific. The document that was sent anonymously to the AAP yesterday was marked for Australian Eyes Only and was meant for Federl Treasurer Peter Costello as he prepares for bilateral meeting with South Pacific countries. Page 1.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Federal Government has been advised to spend A$20 billion on local industry and A$1 billion on promoting investment in an attempt to double growth and match the job creation levels of Asian economies. The recommendations are contained in the Mortimer report, drafted by TNT chief David Mortimer and were released yesterday. Page 1.

Former Western Australian Premier Brian Burke is now a free man after the State's Court of Criminal Appeal overturned his seven convictions of stealing A$122,000 in ALP funds. Burke was sentenced to three years jail in February after being found guilty to stealing A$122,585 in ALP campaign funds between 1984 and 1986 when he was Premier. Page 1.

The Reserve Bank has come under increased pressure to again cut official interest rates after the release of record low inflation rates. Consumer Price Index (CPI) figures for the June quarter show a fall of 0.2 percent in the overall price of consumer items. Page 1.

An e-mail message from Australia's deputy High Commissioner to New Zealand's Ian Lincoln, which contains criticism of the Office of National Assessments (ONA), was leaked to the press yesterday. The ONA, a small group of intelligence officers in the Prime Minister's department prepared the report on South Pacific leaders, which was recently made public in a security breach. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Reserve Bank is expected to announce its fifth cut in official interest rates this year following the dramatic drop in underlying inflation to its lowest levels since records commenced in March 1972. The Consumer Price Index for the June quarter fell by 0.2 percent making the inflation level for the year to June only 0.3 per cent. Page 1.

Ten-year-old Samantha Green was sitting outside her home with several friends, around a lighted candle, when a 54-year-old man approached and splashed methylated spirits over her. Her clothes caught fire as she fled and she is currently recovering in Towsville Hospital from second-and-third degree burns to her back and arms. Page 1.

Former Western Australian Premier Brian Burke has had his convictions on theft charges overturned by the WA Court of Criminal Appeal. In a two-one judgement WA Chief Justice David Malcolm ordered Burke's release from jail ruling there should be no retrial. Page 1.

Real Estate Institute figures show the price of a home in the Sydney suburb of Mosman have risen by 25 percent of over the last financial year to almost A$900,000. In the last June quarter, 70 homes in the lower North Shore suburb were sold with a median price of A$890,000. Page 1.
THE AGE

Federal Industry Minister John Moore said yesterday the Mortimer Review of Business programs, Going for growth, could become the policy base of the Australian economy through to 2010. A central element in the report is the recommendation for a A$1 billion fund to promote competition with Asian countries for foreign investment. Page 1.

The Nine Network owned by Kerry Packer is expected to obtain the rights to screen AFL football on free-to-air and pay-TV when the Seven Network's contract with the AFL ends after the 2001 season. The loss of AFL television rights is likely to downgrade te Seven Network's share price and lead to a loss of advertising revenue. Page 1.

The Western Australia Court of Criminal Appeal has ordered the release from jail of former State Premier Brian Burke after quashing his conviction in February this year on seven counts of stealing A$122,585 from ALP funds. Burke was Premier of Western Autralia for five years until 1988 when he became Australian ambassador to Ireland and the Holy See. Page 1.

Transport workers have decided to hold a 24-hour strike from midnight next Monday that will halt all metropolitan trams, trains and some buses. Secretary of the Public Transport Union Peter Bourke, said the action was necessary in order to highlight the union's dispute with the State Government over pay and redundancy levels. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
